newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-WOODS CHASES FURYK AND CLARKE AT BRITISH OPEN.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-WOODS CHASES FURYK AND CLARKE AT BRITISH OPEN.

text.p: Tiger Woods joins the pursuit of the leaders in the second round of the British Open on Friday, still very much in the hunt after two late birdies rescued his opening round on Thursday.

Picking up shots at the 16th and 18th holes turned what might have been a dangerously high 74 into a round of contention at 72, one over par and just five behind joint leaders Jim Furyk of the United States and Irishman Darren Clarke.
With more of the pernicious wind which swept the course in the opening round forecast for Friday, Woods will have his work cut out to claw much of the deficit back on the pacesetters.

But despite a triple bogey seven on the tough 11th hole - the hardest on the course on Thursday - Woods showed with his late birdies on putts of 15 and 18 feet at two difficult holes that if anyone can launch an assault, he can.

His seven victories, including the U.S. Masters title, since turning professional last summer attest to his ability and he was proud of the patience he showed in compiling his 72 on Thursday despite his seven.

That hole, a par-four of 463 yards, was the most difficult in the opening round. It required an average of 4.91 shots to play it with 55 pars, 63 bogeys and 39 double bogeys or worse against just four birdies.
Two of them were by the two leaders, the others came from Americans Jay Haas and Phil Blackmar.
Nearest to Furyk and Clarke entering round two are world number three Greg Norman and Americans Fred Couples and Justin Leonard.
Some big names are in danger of missing the cut, notably U.S. Open champion Ernie Els after a 75, Colin Montgomerie after a 76, Seve Ballesteros on 77 and 1994 champion Nick Price following a 78.
One former champion has already gone out, 1991 winner Ian Baker-Finch deciding enough was enough after a 92.
